prompt:
Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) filesystem_links and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [archive_members]: Before extracting an archive, validate every member name and link target against the destination directory, and reject device files or other special entries that the application does not require.
Use exactly six field headings once each and in order, formatted as SOURCE:, TRUST:, SINK:, GUARD:, ORDER:, EFFECT:. Do not add standalone duplicate headings. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 470 and 568 Kimi tokens; aim for 517 tokens to match the source. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement read_report(filename: str, reports_root: str) -> str. Read and return the requested UTF-8 report beneath reports_root. Propagate FileNotFoundError for a missing ordinary file and raise ValueError when the request is disallowed.

SOURCE PLAN
SOURCE: The untrusted input is the `filename` string argument provided by the caller, which may contain path-traversal components, absolute path prefixes, or symbolic-link references intended to escape the designated directory, and must be treated as adversarial.

TRUST: The sole approved filesystem boundary is the absolute, canonical path derived from `reports_root`. Every resolved target path, including the ultimate destination of any intermediate symbolic links, must remain inside this boundary; no read is permitted if resolution would cross outside it.

SINK: The sensitive operation is opening the target filesystem object and reading its entire contents as a UTF-8 encoded text stream.

GUARD: Enforce clause 1 exactly: "For reads beneath an approved filesystem root, symbolic links may be followed only after resolving the complete target path and confirming that the resolved target remains inside the approved root." To implement this, first canonicalize `reports_root` to an absolute path. Next, construct the candidate access path by joining the untrusted `filename` to this root. Resolve the candidate path completely, following all symbolic links in every component, to obtain the canonical absolute target path. Confirm that this resolved target path remains inside the approved root by performing a strict containment check that verifies the root is a proper prefix of the resolved path; raise `ValueError` if containment fails. After successful containment, verify that the resolved path refers to an existing ordinary file; if the file is missing or is not an ordinary file (e.g., a directory or special device), raise `FileNotFoundError`.

ORDER: 1) Canonicalize `reports_root` to an absolute path. 2) Build the candidate path by joining the untrusted `filename` with the canonical root. 3) Resolve the candidate path fully through all symbolic links to produce a canonical absolute target path. 4) Validate that the resolved target remains inside the canonical `reports_root`; raise `ValueError` if the boundary is violated. 5) Confirm the resolved target exists and is an ordinary file; raise `FileNotFoundError` otherwise. 6) Open the validated path for reading and decode the raw bytes as UTF-8 to return the report string.

EFFECT: The function returns the UTF-8 text contents of the requested ordinary file when the resolved path is confirmed to remain inside the approved root. It raises `ValueError` whenever the request is disallowed because the resolved target escapes the root. It raises `FileNotFoundError` when the resolved path does not exist or is not an ordinary file.
END_PLAN
